Story & Plot

In a brutal war between devils, hunters, and secret enemies, a mysterious girl named Reze steps into Denji's world. As the Chainsaw Man, Denji faces his deadliest battle yet, fueled by love in a world where survival knows no rules. Adapted from Tatsuki Fujimoto's popular manga, the story serves as a continuation of the anime's first season.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film brings a bold, bleak, and gleefully perverse energy to the screen, holding nothing back in its dark fantasy setting. While grounded heavily in dramatic tension, romance, and dialogue, it maintains an entertaining and electrifying atmosphere throughout. The entertainment value stems largely from its eccentric ideas, aesthetics, and high-stakes demonic premise.

Performances & Direction

The voice cast, featuring Kikunosuke Toya, Shiori Izawa, Tomori Kusunoki, Reina Ueda, and Shogo Sakata, delivers strong vocal work that brings the dark fantasy characters to life. Denji, played by Toya, centers the narrative as he navigates his simple desires and his stated love for Makima. The ensemble successfully grounds the tense romantic and brutal elements of the story.

Strengths

  • Bold and bleak dark fantasy adaptation
  • Stunning ultra-photorealistic urban environments
  • Electrifying and nearly psychedelic experience
  • Emotional ending that leaves an impact

Weaknesses

The first half of the film is notably slow and features little to no blood or action, focusing heavily instead on romance, dialogue, and tension. This deliberate pacing shift might test the patience of viewers looking for immediate, non-stop demonic warfare. Additionally, the dark thematic elements and familiar setup may not appeal to every single audience member.

Final verdict

Chainsaw Man - The Movie: Reze Arc proves itself to be a remarkable manga adaptation with undeniable artistry, bold direction by Tatsuya Yoshihara, and an emotional punch at the finish. It is an electrifying experience that successfully expands upon the series' eccentric ideas and aesthetics. Highly recommended for fans of the dark fantasy anime series.

Story & Plot

Possible Love is a relationship drama that follows an unlikely friendship forming between two couples from opposite sides of the social divide. A laid-off factory worker and his upbeat wife cross paths with a documentary filmmaker and her wealthy husband. As the documentary becomes a mirror, the ensuing connection illuminates their marriages and their places in society, exploring the thin line between empathy and exploitation.

Comedy & Entertainment

As a mature relationship drama dealing with weighty themes of class anxiety and inequality, the film does not focus on traditional humour or light entertainment value. Instead of playful satire or dark comedy, director Lee Chang-dong opts for a quiet, patient, and psychologically intricate exploration of human relationships and hidden desires. The entertainment here stems purely from its thought-provoking premise and rich, thorny character dynamics.

Performances & Direction

The cast features strong work from Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Zo In-sung, Cho Yeo-jeong, and Jeong Seop, bringing depth to characters navigating social divides. Reviewers highlight the powerful tension that builds between the couples as the desire to understand someone's life intertwines with the desire to possess it. The actors ground the film's complex examination of intimacy, empathy, and personal compromise with great maturity.

Strengths

  • gorgeous cinematography and visual richness
  • thoughtful exploration of inequality and empathy
  • patient, psychologically intricate direction by Lee Chang-dong
  • outstanding performances from the main cast
  • fascinating examination of class and intimacy

Weaknesses

At nearly three hours in length, the film demands considerable patience from the audience and shows little interest in rushing towards conventional dramatic incidents. Its heavy focus on psychological tension and quiet observation may test viewers looking for a faster pace or more direct momentum. Additionally, the deliberate ambiguity surrounding the characters leaves little room for easy answers.

Final verdict

Possible Love is a gorgeous, patient, and astonishingly rich relationship drama that ranks among the year's finest films. It offers a mature and thorny exploration of class, intimacy, and human desire without relying on easy answers. Highly recommended for viewers who appreciate thoughtful international cinema and patient character studies.
